text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Serb and Croat members of Bosnia's collective presidency postpone the signing of three World Bank projects on the country's reconstruction for their next session which will be attended by the presidency's Moslem chairman Alija Izetbegovic who is on sick-leave.

- After a bridge was blown up in the northeast Bosnian village of Celic, near the Inter-Entity Boundary Line (IEBL), local Moslem-Croat Federation authorities demand Russian peacekeeping troops patrolling the area be replaced by United States soldiers.
- U.S. companies will not enter bilateral cooperation with Bosnian companies until they get the green light from the U.S. government and its agencies, head of the Bosnian Chamber of Commerce says.
- Governor of Bosnian National Bank, Kasim Omicevic, denies a statement of his Bosnian Serb counterpart and says that there will be only one central bank in Bosnia.
- Another Moslem woman was expelled from the Croat- controlled part of divided the Bosnian town of Mostar, Bosnian police says.
- The Europian Commission (EC) donates 23 new buses for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation and five busses for Bosnian Serb Republic, the EC says in a statement.

- British ambassador to Bosnia, Charles Crawford, denies report that his country exerts influence on decision over the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko and says that Brcko will be resolved through international arbitration.
